regulatory_and_risk_profile: Client outside-counsel guidelines on AI use
paper_process_blockers: Client consent before any third-party AI processes a client matter
Outside-counsel guideline review at each client
Conflicts clearance before a matter is loaded
Partnership vote on firm-wide technology spend
dominant_friction: Billable hours fund the partnership, so tools that speed up work can look like a threat to revenue, and no single leader decides alone.
value_frame: Frame around realization rates, fixed-fee margin expansion, zero-retention ethical walls, and peer-firm competitive pressure.

buying_committee.primary_fear: Associates bill less, partners earn less, and we fund the tool anyway.
We pilot again and nothing reaches the practice groups.
A privileged document leaks into a model's training data.
Our knowledge base fragments across tools that nobody maintains.

signature_objections: If our associates finish in half the time, how do we keep our realization rate intact?
Several of our clients' outside-counsel guidelines ban AI on their matters. How do we stay compliant?
A peer firm just announced an AI rollout. Why should we move slower?

metrics.speaker: Innovation Partner
metrics.setup: Fixed-fee matters are where the partners feel the pressure.
metrics.partial: We have time-saved numbers from the last pilot, but nobody agreed which ones count. The partners think in write-offs and realization.
metrics.verbatim: Fixed-fee margin has to improve on the first three matter types, and realization has to hold at or above where it is today.

economic_buyer.speaker: Managing Partner
economic_buyer.setup: If the partners like this, I can put the technology spend on the agenda.
economic_buyer.partial: The executive committee approves technology spend, but I shape its agenda. The production tier would be a bigger decision.
economic_buyer.verbatim: I can approve a firm-wide pilot up to the technology budget line myself. The production tier needs a partnership vote.

decision_criteria.speaker: General Counsel
decision_criteria.setup: My office vets every vendor on confidentiality, starting with ethical walls and zero retention.
decision_criteria.partial: Both are non-negotiable for my office, so neither is really a tie-breaker.
decision_criteria.verbatim: Anything short of zero retention, no training on our data and matter-level ethical walls. That is disqualifying.

decision_process.speaker: Managing Partner
decision_process.setup: Anything firm-wide eventually goes to the partners.
decision_process.partial: The technology committee looks at it first, and then there is a partnership vote.
decision_process.verbatim: After the technology committee, General Counsel signs off on the walls. Then I take it to the partnership vote.

paper_process.speaker: General Counsel
paper_process.setup: Our biggest clients have rules on AI in their outside-counsel guidelines, and some require consent.
paper_process.partial: We can start, but each client reviews AI usage under its own guidelines, and conflicts have to clear before any matter is loaded.
paper_process.verbatim: Two weeks minimum, for written consent under each client's guidelines and a conflicts clearance.

identify_pain.speaker: Managing Partner
identify_pain.setup: Clients are refusing to pay for a lot of our document review.
identify_pain.partial: Too many associate hours we cannot bill, and peer firms are winning on fixed fees.
identify_pain.verbatim: Write-offs on document review were eleven percent last year, and we keep losing fixed-fee matters because the margin is gone.

champion.speaker: Innovation Partner
champion.setup: I would need to bring the executive committee along before the partners meet in March.
champion.partial: I would sponsor a practice-group trial and argue from the results.
champion.verbatim: Results from the first matter before March. I will sponsor the trial with the litigation group myself.

competition.speaker: Managing Partner
competition.setup: Our partners keep asking what peer firms are doing with AI.
competition.partial: We will not build it ourselves. Two peer firms have already announced tools.
competition.verbatim: One of those peer firms just won our largest client's transactional work with an AI-assisted fixed fee. We cannot wait for a perfect pilot.

veto_holder.reason: A vendor without zero retention and matter-level ethical walls is out, whatever the price.

metrics.open: What number has to move on fixed-fee matters for this to be worth it, and by when?
metrics.pin: How much do you need to cut write-offs, and what realization rate must hold?

economic_buyer.open: Who signs off on technology spend like this, and up to what amount?
economic_buyer.pin: For the production tier, whose budget does this come out of, and who has the final say?

decision_criteria.open: How will you score vendors on ethical walls and zero retention? Which criterion breaks a tie?
decision_criteria.pin: What would rule us out with General Counsel, regardless of price?

decision_process.open: After a successful pilot, what happens on day one, day ten and day thirty for the partnership?
decision_process.pin: Who else needs to approve before the partnership vote? Walk me through the approval path.

paper_process.open: Can your legal team start the client consent process in parallel with the pilot?
paper_process.pin: How long does client consent and conflicts review usually take before a matter is loaded?

identify_pain.open: What does document review that clients refuse to pay for cost you each year?
identify_pain.pin: What happens if you do nothing and peer firms keep winning on fixed fees?

champion.open: If I am not in the room, how would you make the case to the executive committee?
champion.pin: What would you need to take this to the partnership in March with confidence?

competition.open: What happens if you build this in-house, or do nothing while peer firms move?
competition.pin: What are you comparing us against, including the tools peer firms have announced?

account_research.buyer_line: What do you already know about how the firm works?
account_research.strong: I saw the litigation group moved two large clients to fixed fees this year. What prompted that?

discovery_questioning.strong: Walk me through how a contract review gets staffed today, start to finish.

listening_summarizing.buyer_line: One thing before we go on. The bigger issue for us is write-offs on fixed-fee review work, not associate hours.
listening_summarizing.strong: So the real cost is write-offs on fixed-fee review, not associate hours. Did I get that right?

commercial_insight.strong: Firms like yours lose more margin to write-offs on review work than to lost matters. Here is the number.

value_messaging.strong: Today, three associate days per review set. After, half a day, proven with a firm your size.

answer_first.strong: My recommendation: start with the litigation group on fixed-fee review. Three reasons.
